findings.observation: The complete staff remains inside the canvas, but the curled crown begins only about 4–5% below the top and the foot ends about 6% above the bottom, violating the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete staff is shown, including one continuous wooden shaft, curled crown, wrapped grip, and small attached cord fitting; no duplicate object or separate prop appears.
The long hand-height shaft, reinforced grip section, grounded foot, and distinctive but compact natural crown read immediately as a full-length staff.
The staff is a continuous grown wooden form with believable taper and grain direction; tight fibre wraps reinforce the grip and crown junction without implausible joins or top-heavy fittings.
Spiritwood dominates the crown, shaft, grip core, and foot; dark fibre wraps and the small hanging cord remain neutral, subordinate fittings and do not assert another rank.
Continuous twisted grain that follows the shaft and two naturally grown limbs curling into the crown establish spiritwood through physical growth structure beyond palette alone.
Faint blue spirit response is confined to narrow fissures in the upper grown twist; the rest of the staff remains non-emissive and avoids full-object glow.
The image maintains a premium realistic painterly dark-fantasy finish, honest wood and wrap wear, cold key light with restrained warm rim, and a midnight-charcoal floor and background.

Inspection found no transferred person, clothing, hammer, or design; no published-character resemblance, rarity rainbow, gold inflation, object glow, oversized silhouette, ornament-dependent identity, extra gear, text, labels, UI, border, frame, logo, or watermark.
